universe.description: small-cap US stocks with low float (<100M shares, often <20M), gapping up on PR/news

setup.rule: gap scanner for small float small-cap stocks gapping up on news/PR
setup.quote: I have a gap scanner. So with with certain criteria. So I like filter it out by float and market cap. So I want to I want to see a stock with a smaller float like maybe under 100 million. Most of them are like less than 20 million share floats. And you know, I want it to be a small cap.

setup.rule: focus on stocks likely to fail and revert (PR irrelevant, dilution risk)
setup.quote: if you read the PR, if you read the filings, you know that is irrelevant. You know, the PR is completely irrelevant and they're probably going to dilute

entry.rule: scale in short near top with multiple entries (quarter size first), use tape, level 2, dark pools/midpoint
entry.quote: if I for example think, oh this is this is the top and I get in full size and I'm wrong, I take a big loss. Versus if I think, oh this is the top. Let me take a quarter position.

stop.rule: set risk amount; exit if exceeded, avoid stubbornness
stop.quote: I have a set risk amount that I'm willing to lose. If I go past that amount, um stopping myself out and that's it. Sometimes I don't and that's when I take the biggest uh my biggest losses when I get stubborn.

exits.rule: scale out on washouts (cover quarter on sharp drops), short bounces, ride core fade if trend continues
exits.quote: If the stock drops sharply, I want to take some risk off the table because there's probably going to be a bounce. So, I I might take off a quarter. Um if it drops, you know, puts on another two big red candles, then I'm going to take off another quarter.

sizing.rule: scale in/out with quarters or smaller; size down after two red days
sizing.quote: for me it's just sizing down. First thing I do is always I size down. I bring down my my risk for the day, my lockout for the day divided by four automatically.

market_filter.rule: avoid holding into close; focus morning inefficiency
market_filter.quote: I don't really like to trade the close anymore. The close used to be my go-to time, but the market has shifted, and I guess I've adapted to just hit it in the morning and kind of leave it alone for the rest of the day

ambiguities.issue: mentions some long trades in SSR context but primary described method is short fading
